title: Fritto misto di verdure
subtitle: Italian mixed fried vegetables in a light batter
excerpt: Seasonal vegetables (courgette, aubergine, courgette flowers, fennel, and artichoke) dipped in a light beer batter or seasoned flour and fried until golden and crisp. Served immediately with lemon wedges.
sourceNotes: Fritto misto di verdure is a widespread Italian tradition found from Tuscany through to the mezzogiorno. It appears in Ada Boni's Il Talismano della Felicità (1929) and Pellegrino Artusi's La Scienza in Cucina (1891, public domain). The technique of battering and frying seasonal vegetables varies by region: the light beer batter version is associated with northern and central Italian cooking; a semolina or rice flour dip appears in Sicilian cooking.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Vegetables can be prepped and the batter made up to 1 hour ahead. Fry in batches just before serving.

content.text: Fritto misto di verdure is the Italian answer to Japanese tempura: seasonal vegetables in a light, crisp coating, fried quickly at high heat and eaten immediately. The batter is the key. Too thick and the coating overpowers the vegetable; too thin and it does not protect the vegetable from the oil. A cold beer batter made just before frying is the most reliable method for consistently light results.

items.prepNote: cut into 1 cm rounds or batons
small bulb, outer leaves removed, cut into 5 mm wedges through the root
ice cold; or use a cold light beer

content.text: Make the batter: whisk the flour and salt together. Add the ice-cold sparkling water (or beer) and whisk until just combined. A few small lumps are fine; do not overwork it. Refrigerate the batter for 30 minutes.
Heat the oil to 180°C in a large, deep, heavy pan.

Working in batches, dip the vegetables in the cold batter, letting any excess drip off, and lower into the hot oil. Fry for 2 to 3 minutes until golden and crisp on all sides. Lift out with a slotted spoon and drain on kitchen paper. Season immediately with sea salt flakes.
Serve immediately on a plate lined with kitchen paper, with lemon wedges. Fritto misto must be eaten straight from the pan.

items.cause: Too much flour or batter not cold enough
items.fix: The batter should be the consistency of single cream. Add more cold sparkling water to thin it. Keep the batter and the vegetables cold right up to the point of frying.

items.cause: Vegetables were wet, or oil not hot enough
items.fix: Dry vegetables thoroughly before dipping. Check the oil temperature reaches 180°C before each batch.

content.text: Fritto misto di verdure appears across Italian cuisine, with regional variations in which vegetables are chosen and how the batter or coating is made. In Tuscany it appears as part of the broader fritto misto spread, which also includes offal, cheese, and fresh fruit. In Liguria and Veneto it is a summer dish of market-fresh courgettes, sage leaves, and courgette flowers. In Sicily the coating tends toward semolina or plain flour rather than a wet batter. The common thread is freshness, speed, and serving at once: cold fritto misto is a different and much lesser thing.
